notes: 1212-DIN is a 1-input, 12-output DMX512/RDM isolated splitter/distribution amplifier for DIN-rail mounting (2"H x 4.25"D x 6"W, 10 oz). Two other SKUs exist with identical electronics but different enclosures: 1212-DIN-JBOX (installed in a NEMA 1 junction box) and 1212-DIN-JBOX-PS (junction box plus bundled PSDIN-30W-24V power supply) — this spec reflects the base bare 1212-DIN DIN-rail unit. All signal and power connectors are pluggable screw-type Phoenix terminal blocks (modeled here as "euroblock"/"euroblock-dc"), not XLR — this is a permanent-install/rack-room device, not a stage-cabled unit. No connector on this device carries a versioned bandwidth grade (DMX512 is a fixed-rate protocol), so no "grade" values were set. Exact per-terminal silkscreen numbering for the 12 outputs could not be confirmed from the extracted datasheet text (only that they total 12 across three 12-position terminal blocks); everything else (input isolation, power range/wattage, connector style, LED indicators, environmental/mounting specs) is directly quoted from Doug Fleenor Design's official technical data sheet.

ports.name: DMX/RDM Input
ports.note: 3-position pluggable Phoenix terminal block; fully opto-isolated to 1500V. The splitter is RDM-capable and bi-directional overall, so RDM responses from fixtures return to the console over this same terminal block; primary signal flow is console-to-splitter.

ports.name: Output 12
ports.note: The 12 outputs are wired across three 12-position pluggable Phoenix terminal blocks (4 output circuits x 3 pins per block, DMX+/DMX-/common); each is separately driven but not isolated from one another. Datasheet text does not confirm the exact silkscreen numbering scheme, so 1-12 labeling here is inferred from the '12 output' product description.

ports.name: Power
ports.note: 2-position pluggable Phoenix terminal block. Accepts 9-24 VDC, 10W low-voltage DC. Panel is silkscreened '24 VDC 10W' near the terminal in product photos. DFD's optional matched external supply is model PSDIN-30W-24V (24VDC output); user-supplied DC power is also acceptable.
